cards.text: Paul is writing to the church in Thessalonica, with Silvanus and Timothy right beside him (2 Thess 1:1). He just finished praying for these believers, asking God to encourage their hearts (2 Thess 2:16-17). Now he starts wrapping up with 'Finally, brothers,' and friend, I say 'finally' at the oven every night, and somehow there's ALWAYS three more batches.

cards.question: Paul just prayed for the believers in Thessalonica. Now that he's wrapping up, what does he ask them to do for him and his team?

cards.text: And look at the first thing on Paul's list. It's not a nicer bed or a smoother road. It's the word of the Lord.

cards.question: Paul asks the believers in Thessalonica to pray about the word of the Lord. What does he want to happen with it?

answers.text: It spreads quickly and is honored
It stays hidden until the right time
It is kept among the church leaders

cards.question: Paul says the word of the Lord was already held in honor among the believers in Thessalonica.

cards.text: Then comes prayer request number two. This one is about Paul's team getting rescued.

cards.question: Paul asks the believers in Thessalonica to pray that his team will be delivered. Delivered from what?
Paul explains why his team runs into wicked and evil men: not everyone holds to the ___.

cards.text: Not everyone holds to the faith. Then Paul turns it around: 'But the Lord is faithful.' Baker, that's my whole junk drawer story in five words. Everybody forgot about me. HE didn't.

cards.question: Paul says the Lord is faithful. What does he say the Lord will do for the believers in Thessalonica?

answers.text: Strengthen and guard them from the evil one
Take away every trouble in their lives
Bring Paul back to stay with them

cards.text: Next, Paul tells the believers he's confident about them. But watch where he puts that confidence.

cards.question: Paul says his confidence is in the ___ that the believers will do what he commands.
Paul says the believers in Thessalonica are already doing what he commands, and will continue to do it.

cards.text: Confidence in the Lord, not in their willpower. Smart. I put my confidence in MY willpower once. The snooze button won. Eleven times. ELEVEN.
Earlier in this letter, Paul wrote that these believers are enduring persecutions and afflictions (2 Thess 1:4). Now he prays for their hearts: 'May the Lord direct your hearts…'

cards.question: Paul prays the Lord will direct the believers' hearts into something of Christ's. What is it?
Paul also prays the Lord will direct the believers' hearts into God's love.
